record.question: 'Tungchaw' literally means
record.explanation: The 1913 Lushai-English dictionary (Lorrain & Savidge) lists 'Tung-chaw, (n.) a Lushai bedpost' (and 'Tung-chaw-kua', a hole in a Lushai bedpost), so the term literally denotes the traditional Mizo bedpost - 'tung' being the bed post and 'chaw' the Lushai word for rice/food, the bed being a bamboo one.
